observations: SCOREBOARD. with_skill 14/14 assertions (eval2 8/8, eval4 6/6). without_skill 13/14 (eval2 7/8, eval4 6/6). But only 1 of 14 assertion-pairs actually discriminated: eval2 #6 (ambiguity in 'account-verification') went to the skill. Eval 4 discriminated on nothing at all.

LENGTH FIXES WORKED, AND SHORTER IS NOT WORSE. Eval 4 fell from 1818 words (iteration 2) to 602 (baseline 604) and still scored 6/6; eval 2 fell from 2056 to 990. What was cut was apparatus, not content — no lens names, no cluster analysis, no diversity score, no process narration appears in either deliverable. The eval-4 with_skill answer at 602 words is if anything sharper than the 604-word baseline (pause-to-reveal-latent-demand, threshold-firing on accumulated signal, 'make the recording deliberately worse than the room' vs the baseline's 'Shrink it' and 'Rotate the stage'). Length is also not tracking quality in the obvious direction: on eval 2 the with_skill answer is 184 words LONGER than the baseline (990 vs 806) and still won the one discriminating assertion.

ONE REAL LOSS FROM THE LENGTH FIX. Eval 2's user_notes admits the budget forced a cut: 'First draft was 1025 words with 6 ideas ... "inherit the proof" (passkey/SSO/vouch) was dropped to the cut list', described in the same note as 'arguably the most immediately actionable of the six'. The baseline offers SSO as a live recommendation ('Offer Google/Apple/Microsoft SSO. Those accounts arrive pre-verified'). So on that specific item the shorter skill output is worse, and the loss was caused by the budget, not by judgement about the idea.

DIAGNOSIS-FIRST FIRED CORRECTLY ON 2 AND 4 BUT PRODUCED NO LIFT. Both with_skill runs open with candidate causes before ideas — but so do both baselines, unprompted. Eval 2 baseline's four-way split (never received / received but never opened / opened but didn't complete / never got that far) is near-identical to the skill's four candidate causes, and eval 4 baseline separates 'low information value / low stakes / friction' with a who-is-missing test. Assertions 1 and 2 on eval 2 and assertions 3 and 6 on eval 4 all passed for both configs. Diagnosis-first is codifying what a competent plain answer already does; its value is insurance against a bad run, not marginal quality.

DIVERSITY.PY IS CEREMONY IN FAST MODE. It scored 9.91/10 (eval 2) and 9.90/10 with 'no pairs above 0.22' (eval 4) and, per the notes, 'caught nothing'; the real deduplication was the operator's own mechanism-level merge. That matches the user's complaint. Recommendation: drop it from fast mode entirely, and in deep mode either rename its output ('lexical overlap only — this is not a mechanism-diversity score') or replace it with a mechanism-level check.

THE DIAGNOSIS BLOCK VS THE 600-WORD BUDGET IS A GENUINE CONFLICT AND THE USER IS RIGHT. Eval 4's notes: the diagnosis block cost '~170 words — nearly 30% of the budget — leaving room for roughly four ideas against a template that says 4-8'. Given that diagnosis-first discriminated on nothing in this iteration (both baselines did it unprompted), spending 30% of a light-question budget on it is a bad trade. Either charge the diagnosis block against the budget explicitly and lower the idea count to 3-4 for light questions, or cap it at ~80 words / three causes with one test each.

BIOMIMICRY COLLIDES WITH THE FAST-MODE NO-SEARCH RULE — MARK IT DEEP-ONLY. The lens requires an organism plus a verifiable mechanism, while Phase 3 step 4 forbids presenting an unverified outside claim in fast mode. Net effect on eval 4 was a de-cited principle: 'threshold-triggered firing, stripped of the quorum-sensing citation'. That is a lens contributing nothing a plain inversion pass wouldn't have produced. Same pattern in eval 2, where the emergency-intake grounding for 'temporary identifier' had to be stated 'as a shape rather than a sourced fact'.

ONE OTHER PROCESS COMPLAINT WORTH ACTING ON. Eval 4's notes report that fast mode's 'separate labelled passes' leak vocabulary — 'the Phase 2 negation round did more real work than passes 4-5 did ... fast mode might do better with three lenses plus two negation rounds than five lenses plus one'. Cheap to test.

MODE SELECTION IS NOW SOLID. Both with_skill runs picked the right mode and the metrics confirm it: eval 2 fast (0 subagents, 0 searches, 14 calls), eval 4 fast (0 subagents, 0 searches, 13 calls). Both MODE CHECK assertions passed. The iteration-1 failure — deep mode firing on a bounded problem — did not recur, and eval 2's notes show the gate being applied explicitly ('One condition -> fast'), correctly refusing to let 'the user is stuck' alone trigger deep.

EVAL 4 NO LONGER EARNS ITS PLACE AS AN EVAL. Identical scores (6/6 vs 6/6), near-identical lengths (602 vs 604), same mode behaviour, same diagnosis-first structure. The skill produces a better answer on inspection — weirder, more mechanism-diverse options — but no assertion in the set can detect it. Either add an assertion that bites (e.g. 'at least one option would be uncomfortable to propose to leadership', or 'no option is a format/duration/presenter change') or retire it. Eval 2 is close to the same problem: 7 of 8 assertions are non-discriminating and the entire margin rests on ambiguity disclosure.
